findings.requirement: NBFCs must give adequate notice to borrowers or legal heirs through available communication channels to repay or settle loan dues prior to initiating the auction procedure.

regulation.label: Responsible Business Conduct Directions, 2025 | G. Conduct related aspects in Lending Against Gold and Silver Collateral > G.5 Release of Collateral after Repayment | paras 57-60
regulation.quote: An NBFC shall give adequate notice to the borrower(s)/ legal heir(s), as applicable, through available means of communication to repay or settle the loan dues prior to initiating the auction procedure.

policy.label: IIFL Finance Limited - Fair Practices Code | I. Loans
policy.quote: The loan agreement for lending against gold shall disclose details regarding auction procedure. The Company shall follow transparent auction procedure in case of nonrepayment with adequate prior notice to the borrower.

findings.explanation: The policy commits to providing adequate prior notice to the borrower before auctioning gold collateral, but it omits notice to legal heirs where applicable and does not explicitly state the purpose of giving notice to settle or repay dues through available communication channels.

findings.requirement: NBFCs must announce gold and silver collateral auctions to the public by issuing advertisements in at least two newspapers, one in the regional language and another in a national daily.

regulation.label: Responsible Business Conduct Directions, 2025 | G. Conduct related aspects in Lending Against Gold and Silver Collateral > G.6 Transparency in Auction Procedure | paras 60-62
regulation.quote: An NBFC shall implement a transparent auction procedure, which shall include, inter alia, announcement of the auction to the public by issue of advertisements in at least two newspapers, one in the regional language and another in a national daily.

policy.label: IIFL Finance Limited - Fair Practices Code | T.Lending against collateral of Gold Jewellery
policy.quote: The auction shall be announced to the public by issue of advertisements in at least two newspapers, one in vernacular and another in national daily newspaper

findings.explanation: The policy commits to announcing public auctions via advertisements in at least two newspapers, including one vernacular (regional language) and one national daily.

findings.requirement: Pledged collateral must be auctioned only through an experienced or trained NBFC employee or an empanelled auctioneer, applying internal safeguards if conducted through employees.

regulation.label: Responsible Business Conduct Directions, 2025 | G. Conduct related aspects in Lending Against Gold and Silver Collateral > G.6 Transparency in Auction Procedure | paras 61-64
regulation.quote: The pledged eligible collateral shall be auctioned by an NBFC only through its employee having necessary experience and / or training or an auctioneer empanelled by the NBFC as per its policy.

policy.label: IIFL Finance Limited - Fair Practices Code | T.Lending against collateral of Gold Jewellery
policy.quote: Gold pledged shall be auctioned only through auctioneers approved by the Board

findings.explanation: The policy requires pledged gold to be auctioned exclusively through Board-approved auctioneers, satisfying the regulatory requirement allowing auctions via empanelled auctioneers.

findings.requirement: NBFCs must set a reserve price for collateral at auction of at least 90 percent of current value, or at least 85 percent if auctions fail twice.

regulation.label: Responsible Business Conduct Directions, 2025 | G. Conduct related aspects in Lending Against Gold and Silver Collateral > G.6 Transparency in Auction Procedure | paras 61-64
regulation.quote: An NBFC shall declare a reserve price for the gold and silver collateral at the time of auction, which shall not be less than 90 per cent of its current value. Provided that in case auctions fail twice, a reserve price not less than 85 per cent of its current value shall be adopted.

findings.explanation: While the policy excerpts cover general auction transparency, public advertisements, and board-approved auctioneers, they do not mention setting a reserve price of at least 90 percent of current value (or 85 percent if auctions fail twice).

findings.requirement: The first auction must take place physically in the lending branch's district, but if it fails, the NBFC may auction in an adjoining district or online.

regulation.label: Responsible Business Conduct Directions, 2025 | G. Conduct related aspects in Lending Against Gold and Silver Collateral > G.6 Transparency in Auction Procedure | paras 63-66
regulation.quote: The first auction shall be conducted physically in the same district in which the lending branch is located. However, in case of failure of first auction, an NBFC may conduct the auction in an adjoining district or conduct online auction.

findings.explanation: The provided excerpts outline general auction rules (such as newspaper advertisements and approved auctioneers) but do not state that the first auction must be held physically in the lending branch's district or specify the conditions for holding auctions in an adjoining district or online.

findings.requirement: Any surplus proceeds from the auction of gold or silver collateral must be refunded to the borrower or legal heir within seven working days of receipt.

regulation.label: Responsible Business Conduct Directions, 2025 | G. Conduct related aspects in Lending Against Gold and Silver Collateral > G.6 Transparency in Auction Procedure | paras 66-68
regulation.quote: The surplus, if any, from the auction of the gold or silver collateral, shall be refunded to the borrower(s) / legal heir(s) within a maximum period of seven working days from the date of receipt of the full auction proceeds.

findings.explanation: The provided excerpts outline several requirements for transparent gold auction procedures, but do not mention the refund of surplus auction proceeds or the mandatory seven-working-day timeline for refunding them to the borrower or legal heir.

Nissan Renault | penal charges on loans.policy_title: Nissan Renault Financial Services India Private Limited - Fair Practices Code

findings.requirement: Penalties for non-compliance with loan terms must be levied as penal charges rather than penal interest added to the interest rate, and penal charges must not be capitalized.

regulation.label: Responsible Business Conduct Directions, 2025 | Chapter III – Responsible Lending Conduct > C. Penal Charges in Loan Accounts | para 30
regulation.quote: Penalty, if charged, for non-compliance of material terms and conditions of loan contract by the borrower shall be treated as ‘penal charges’ and shall not be levied in the form of ‘penal interest’ that is added to the rate of interest charged on the advances.

policy.label: Nissan Renault Financial Services India Private Limited - Fair Practices Code | 1.INTRODUCTION > 7.LOAN APPRAISAL AND TERMS/CONDITIONS
policy.quote: The Company shall mention the penal interest charged for late repayment in bold in the loan agreement.

findings.explanation: The policy provides for charging 'penal interest' for late repayment, which directly contradicts the regulatory mandate requiring penalties to be levied as penal charges and not as penal interest.

findings.requirement: The NBFC must formulate a Board-approved policy on penal charges or similar charges on loans.

regulation.label: Responsible Business Conduct Directions, 2025 | Chapter III – Responsible Lending Conduct > C. Penal Charges in Loan Accounts | para 30
regulation.quote: The NBFC shall formulate a Board approved policy on penal charges or similar charges on loans, by whatever name called.

findings.explanation: The excerpts mention disclosing penal interest in bold within loan agreements and framing internal principles on charges, but do not mention formulating a Board-approved policy on penal charges or similar charges.

findings.requirement: The quantum of penal charges must be reasonable, commensurate with non-compliance of material loan terms, and non-discriminatory within a particular loan or product category.

regulation.label: Responsible Business Conduct Directions, 2025 | Chapter III – Responsible Lending Conduct > C. Penal Charges in Loan Accounts | para 30
regulation.quote: The quantum of penal charges shall be reasonable and commensurate with the non-compliance of material terms and conditions of loan contract without being discriminatory within a particular loan / product category.

findings.explanation: The policy mentions disclosing penal interest in bold and ensuring charges are not excessive, but does not address the requirement that penal charges must be reasonable, commensurate with non-compliance of material loan terms, and non-discriminatory across loan categories.

findings.requirement: For loans sanctioned to individual borrowers for non-business purposes, penal charges must not exceed those applicable to non-individual borrowers for similar non-compliance.

regulation.label: Responsible Business Conduct Directions, 2025 | Chapter III – Responsible Lending Conduct > C. Penal Charges in Loan Accounts | para 30
regulation.quote: The penal charges in case of loans sanctioned to ‘individual borrowers, for purposes other than business’, shall not be higher than the penal charges applicable to non-individual borrowers for similar non-compliance of material terms and conditions.

findings.explanation: The policy excerpts do not address the requirement that penal charges for individual borrowers for non-business purposes must not exceed those applicable to non-individual borrowers for similar non-compliance.

findings.requirement: The NBFC must clearly disclose the quantum and reason for penal charges upfront in the loan agreement, Most Important Terms & Conditions or Key Fact Statement, and on its website.

regulation.label: Responsible Business Conduct Directions, 2025 | Chapter III – Responsible Lending Conduct > C. Penal Charges in Loan Accounts | para 30
regulation.quote: The quantum and reason for penal charges shall be clearly disclosed by the NBFC to the customers upfront in the loan agreement and Most Important Terms & Conditions/ Key Fact Statement as applicable, in addition to being displayed on the NBFC’s website

policy.label: Nissan Renault Financial Services India Private Limited - Fair Practices Code | 1.INTRODUCTION > 7.LOAN APPRAISAL AND TERMS/CONDITIONS
policy.quote: The Company shall mention the penal interest charged for late repayment in bold in the loan agreement.

findings.explanation: The policy only commits to mentioning penal interest for late repayment in bold within the loan agreement. It fails to require disclosing both the quantum and reason for penal charges in the MITC/KFS or displaying them on the company's website.

findings.requirement: The NBFC must communicate applicable penal charges when sending non-compliance reminders to borrowers, and also communicate any instance and reason for levying penal charges.

regulation.label: Responsible Business Conduct Directions, 2025 | Chapter III – Responsible Lending Conduct > C. Penal Charges in Loan Accounts | para 30
regulation.quote: Whenever reminders for non-compliance of material terms and conditions of loan are sent to borrowers, the applicable penal charges shall be communicated. Further, any instance of levy of penal charges and the reason thereof shall also be communicated.

findings.explanation: The provided excerpts do not address the requirement to communicate applicable penal charges in non-compliance reminders or to communicate specific instances and reasons for levying penal charges.
